head: Create a square 1:1 image. tail: No scenery, no text, no watermark, no sun symbol, no Japanese or Chinese style clothing, no Chinese hairpins or court robes.
g-31-buyeo-geumha: Geumha, the aging king of Buyeo in the snowy north of ancient Korea, in his late fifties, a long dignified black beard streaked with grey, heavy-lidded calculating eyes that weigh every word, a tall white fur hat trimmed with small gold and silver plaques, a heavy black sable fur mantle over a plain white hemp jeogori (Buyeo people wore white), a string of red carnelian and amber beads, one hand resting on the hilt of an iron sword.
g-33-jeoga-metdol: Metdol, the boar-clan chief (Jeoga) of Buyeo in ancient Korea, about 40, a huge hairy brawler with a broad battered face, a wild black beard and a fierce laughing grin, shaggy hair in a loose messy topknot, a whole black wild-boar hide over his shoulders with the tusked boar head resting on one shoulder, a torn white hemp jeogori over a massive chest, a boar-tusk necklace, a heavy iron axe gripped low.
g-37-eumjeup-jeup: Jeup, the jolly farmer chieftain of Eumjeupbeol, a small Jinhan state of ancient Korea (Angang), about 50, a round tanned face with plump red cheeks, a thin moustache and a beaming squinting smile, hair in a small topknot, a woven straw hat hanging on his back, a loose undyed hemp jeogori tied with a cord sash, a long string of green jade and red clay beads, holding a gourd bottle in one hand and ripe barley ears in the other.
g-39-guya-soebo: Soebo, the iron-smith king (Jinjiryeom) of Guya, the iron kingdom of Garak (Gimhae) in ancient Korea, late forties, a stern square face with a dark beard flecked with grey and an old burn mark on one cheek, hair in a topknot under a gilt-bronze Gaya crown with upright tree-branch prongs, a dark bear-fur mantle over riveted iron plate armor of Gaya style, a large green jade comma bead on a cord, holding up a freshly forged iron ring-pommel sword.
g-40-anya-adan: Adan, the careful chieftain (Sinji) of Anya, the Ara Gaya state of ancient Korea (Haman), about 35, lean and handsome with cool watchful eyes and a faint knowing smile, a few loose strands of hair falling from a neat topknot, a charcoal-black hemp jeogori with narrow sleeves and an ochre collar band tied with a sash, a strand of pale crystal and dark beads, holding a grey stoneware pedestal cup with flame-shaped cutouts in its stem (Ara Gaya pottery).
g-72-gyeonji-soeul: Soeul, a wandering blacksmith captain (Gyeonji) of the Samhan in ancient Korea, about 40, bronzed and muscular with a short rough beard and a booming confident grin, hair in a tight topknot, a sleeveless frayed olive hemp vest under a scorched leather smith's apron, leather wrist wraps, a small bronze tag on a cord at his neck, a heavy iron sledgehammer resting on one shoulder.
l-L5-seonyeo: Seonyeo (Se-onyeo), the legendary weaver woman of the eastern seashore of Silla in ancient Korea, whose silk held the light of the heavens, about 25, a round soft cheerful face with dimples and a sweet crescent-eyed smile, plump and warm, a long thick braid wound with a pale blue ribbon, a cream hemp jeogori over a deep navy skirt, holding up a length of shimmering pale silk that glows with soft silvery moonlight and tiny drifting stars.
l-L6-jeonggyeon-moju: Jeonggyeon-moju, the mountain goddess of Gayasan, mother of the first kings of Gaya in ancient Korea, a mature beauty in her thirties, tall and stately with serene knowing eyes and a calm half smile, long black hair in many thin braids threaded with small iron rings, a thin bronze circlet on her brow, a mantle of layered green pine needles over a deep green jeogori with an ochre collar and a bronze-plaqued belt, wisps of mountain mist curling around her shoulders.
l-L8-nangnang-princess: The Princess of Nangnang, the ancient Korean kingdom of Nangnang, who tore open the self-sounding war drum for her love Prince Hodong of Goguryeo, about 18, a delicate pale beautiful face with a single tear running down her cheek and resolute trembling lips, black hair in a long loose braid tied with a red cord (no bun), a deep crimson jeogori with a fine white dotted pattern and a black collar band, gripping a small bronze knife against her chest, the slashed leather drumhead of a painted drum beside her shoulder.
l-L9-ungnyeo: Ungnyeo, the bear woman of the Dangun founding myth of ancient Korea, who became human by eating mugwort and garlic in a cave, about 25, tanned skin and strong muscular shoulders, untamed thick wavy black hair tucked with green mugwort sprigs, steady proud dark eyes, a brown bear-fur shawl over an earthy green hemp jeogori, a bear-claw necklace, holding a bundle of mugwort and a few garlic bulbs, a faint golden ghost of a bear glowing behind her.
l-L10-pyeonggang: Princess Pyeonggang of Goguryeo in ancient Korea, who married the humble Ondal and made him a great general, about 20, a slim feline beauty with sharp cat-like eyes, a playful wink and a teasing smile, a high black ponytail with two upright pheasant feathers, a red jeogori with a fine dotted pattern in Goguryeo mural style slipping off one shoulder, leather bracers, drawing a short Korean maekgung recurve bow back to her cheek.
w-07-shaman-queen: A shaman queen of a Mahan state in ancient Korea, keeper of the sacred grove, about 30, an ethereal pale beauty with closed eyes in deep trance and a still calm mouth, very long loose black hair drifting as if in an unseen wind, a black hemp jeogori embroidered with bronze-gold swirl patterns, a large round bronze mirror with fine crosshatched triangle line patterns on her chest, many strands of green jade comma beads, holding a bronze eight-bell rattle.
w-08-mahan-warrior: Iseul, a laughing wanderer warrior and night trader of Mahan in ancient Korea, late twenties, beautiful with tanned skin, sparkling eyes that see in the dark and a wide joyous open-mouthed laugh, curly black hair piled up in a messy bun, swirling Mahan tattoos on her bare shoulder and arm, a dark teal sleeveless hemp top crossed by leather straps, a small rectangular bronze plaque and green beads at her neck, a long iron spear over her shoulder.
w-09-byeonhan-smith: Danbi, a cheerful smith and farm woman wanderer of Byeonhan in ancient Korea, mid-twenties, pretty with soft freckles, a smudge of soot on her cheek and a tipsy crooked grin, black hair in a loose bun with stray strands, a sleeveless cream hemp top under a battered leather smith's apron, leather gloves, a small gourd of rice wine hanging from her belt, holding iron tongs over her shoulder.
w-11-assassin: Sori, a cold silent assassin of the Samhan in ancient Korea, about 25, a sharp beautiful face fully visible with narrow night-seeing eyes and a hard unsmiling mouth, short black hair under a dark indigo head cloth (dugeon) knotted at the back, a fitted charcoal hemp jeogori with narrow sleeves tied with a dark sash, a dark leather vest, raising a short single-edged iron knife beside her cheek, a short Korean maekgung bow slung across her back.
w-12-court-dancer: Nari, a charming wandering dancer (Eupcha) of ancient Korea, about 22, lovely with a sweet heart-shaped face, a coy sidelong smile and bright almond eyes, black hair in a braided crown wound with small gilt-bronze leaf ornaments, a red jeogori with a white dotted pattern and a woven zigzag collar band, long white dancing scarves swirling around her arms and shoulders in mid-turn.
w-14-feast-spy: Noeul, a nervous feast spy wanderer of the Samhan in ancient Korea, about 24, pretty with straight bangs, darting watchful eyes and an uneasy polite smile, long straight black hair under a dark navy head cloth (dugeon) tied at the nape, a dark navy jeogori with narrow sleeves and a black sash, strands of red and blue glass beads, holding a bronze wine cup at a feast, the iron handle of a short knife peeking from her sleeve.
w-16-clan-matriarch: A stern clan matriarch of a noble house in ancient Korea, about 55, a handsome strong-boned face with fine wrinkles, shrewd hooded eyes and a thin unbending smile, grey-streaked black hair braided and coiled low at the nape with no ornaments, a deep indigo silk jeogori with a dark grey collar band and a simple woven cloud pattern trim, a long necklace of green jade comma beads, small dark jade earrings, hands folded.
w-47-gosaburi-baram: Baram, the careful wind-reading chieftess (Eupcha) of Gosaburi, a Mahan state of ancient Korea (Jeongeup), about 30, lean and striking with long windswept black hair and calm narrowed eyes, a slight sly smile, a long cream scarf streaming in the wind, a dark teal jeogori with a grey collar band tied with a sash, strands of pale stone beads, holding a small carved wooden bird (sotdae bird) in one hand, a short bronze dagger at her hip.
w-48-mujin-mudeung: Mudeung, the stubborn mountain chieftess (Eupcha) of Mujin, a Mahan state of ancient Korea (Gwangju, Mudeung mountain), mid-forties, handsome weathered face with fine laugh lines and a steady unyielding gaze, a thick grey-streaked braid wrapped around her neck, a shaggy deerskin fur vest over a moss-green jeogori, strands of green and amber beads, an iron spear with hanging hawk feathers held upright beside her.
w-49-goryong-gureum: Gureum, the charming cloud-soft chieftess (Eupcha) of Goryong, a Mahan state of ancient Korea, mid-twenties, beautiful with a playful wink, red lips and a dimpled smile, long wavy black hair strewn with tiny white pearls, small silver drop earrings, a white hemp jeogori with a pale sky-blue collar band, a pearl necklace, raising a small bronze wine cup as if in a toast.
w-51-haseulla-dangung: Dangung, the archer chieftess (Samno) of Haseulla, a Dongye state of ancient Korea (Gangneung), about 30, fierce and beautiful with hunter's narrowed eyes and a confident smirk, a long high black braid bound with leopard fur, a leopard pelt over one shoulder above a deep red jeogori, leather bracers, drawing back a short birchwood dangung bow with an arrow nocked, aiming past the viewer.
w-52-biryuna-songbi: Songbi, the proud young chieftess (Paeja) of Biryuna in early Goguryeo, daughter of King Songyang, about 19, lovely with a fair rosy face, bold bright eyes and a spirited smile (no forehead mark), black hair coiled in a thick braided crown tied with a red ribbon, gold drop earrings, a mustard-yellow jeogori with a black dotted pattern and a wine-red collar band in Goguryeo mural style, a green bead necklace, a short maekgung bow in hand.
w-53-hwanna-gabi: Gabi, the shrewd trader chieftess (Paeja) of Hwanna in early Goguryeo, about 30, beautiful with smoky eyes, a sharp jaw and a sly bargaining smile, long black hair worked with many thin braids strung with small colored beads, small gold hoop earrings, a dark green jeogori with a white dotted pattern and an orange collar band, layered necklaces of amber, orange and blue beads, a red fox fur draped over one shoulder.
w-55-guga-nuri: Nuri, the charming dog-clan chieftess (Guga) of Buyeo in ancient Korea, about 22, sweet and elegant with gentle doe eyes and a soft knowing smile, long straight black hair half tied up with a small white fur puff, gold leaf earrings, a white Buyeo jeogori with a thick white fur collar, a gold dog-shaped pendant and pearl beads, holding a fluffy white hunting puppy in her arms.
w-56-dongokjeo-sogeum: Sogeum, the salt and fish trader chieftess of East Okjeo on the east sea of ancient Korea, about 50, a handsome weathered face with sharp shrewd eyes and a tight-lipped half smile, grey-streaked black hair in two thick braids coiled at the sides, a spotted seal-fur cape fastened with a bronze clasp over a deep blue jeogori, a necklace of rough white salt-crystal and dark stone beads, holding a small wooden box heaped with coarse white sea salt.
w-79-yangmaek-solmae: Solmae, a quiet river-guide woman general of Yangmaek, the Maek people of the Amnok river valleys in ancient Korea, about 24, a striking angular face with high cheekbones, calm deep eyes and a faint serious frown, black hair in two long braids with a pine sprig tucked behind one ear, a shaggy fur vest over a dark dotted jeogori, a short maekgung bow on her back and a dried river fish hanging at her hip.
